Pasting invalid JSON shows a red error message. The browser's parser reports the approximate location and cause — a missing comma, a wrong quote or an extra brace — so you find the problem in large data sets within seconds.

Generating and checking sample data while writing scripts.

No. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption — it does not hide data, it only makes it portable. Never rely on Base64 alone to protect passwords or private information; use real encryption for sensitive data.
Yes. Both operations run in your browser; your data is never sent or stored. No signup and completely free.

It uses encodeURIComponent, the recommended comprehensive encoding for parameter values. Every character except A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and a few marks becomes percent notation, so browsers and servers always read your parameters identically.
Yes. Encoding and decoding happen entirely in your browser; inputs are never sent or stored. No signup, no install and completely free.

Legacy systems: older databases and APIs still reference MD5 for identification and deduplication.

md5-hash.h: What is MD5 used for today?
md5-hash.p: MD5 still works as a fast integrity check: verify that a downloaded file matches its published checksum, or detect accidental corruption in transfers. It is built into many systems, which is why you will keep seeing it in logs and package metadata.

MD5 is designed to be fast, and fast hashing is exactly what password crackers want. Modern hardware restores simple MD5 hashes in seconds, so passwords should be stored with slow, salted algorithms instead. Use the SHA hash tools when a one-way cryptographic digest is needed.

date-difference.h: What is a Date Difference calculator?
date-difference.p: A Date Difference calculator splits the duration between two dates into years, months and days, and also shows the total in days, weeks, hours and minutes. It saves time for birthdays, contract deadlines, tenure and project timelines — whichever date comes first, the absolute difference is shown.

date-difference.h: How should you read the result?
date-difference.p: The years/months/days conversion is based on calendar averages (365.2425 days per year) and gives a satisfying "how long" perspective. Total days and hours are exact and should be the basis for calculations that need precision, like contract periods.
Yes. The calculation happens entirely in your browser; your dates are never sent or stored. No signup, no install and completely free.

list: Does date order matter? No — the absolute difference is shown.
Can the start date be today? Yes — fields default to today.
Are total hours realistic? Yes — exact days multiplied by 24.

color-converter.p: A Color Converter instantly converts between HEX, RGB and HSL notations. Web developers constantly need to align colors across designs, mobile interfaces and graphics programs. This tool also previews the color and lets you copy any format with one click.

list: HEX: the standard in web design — #RRGGBB six-digit hex notation.
RGB: three numbers 0–255 used by screens and graphics software; the basis of contrast math.
HSL: hue, saturation and lightness make adjustments like "lighter" or "darker" natural.

color-converter.p: Yes. All conversions run in your browser; your color is never sent anywhere. Fast access without fees, memberships or ad filters.

list: Do I need the # prefix for HEX? Either works — both 6-digit forms are accepted.
Which field updates the color? The last valid input applies; invalid entries keep the current color.
Are the HSL percentages required? Yes — saturation and lightness need the % sign.

uuid-generator.p: A UUID (universally unique identifier) is a standard 128-bit identifier written in 36 characters, e.g. 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000. Version 4 is produced randomly, making collisions practically impossible across distributed systems, databases and APIs.

list: Database primary keys and record identifiers.
API trace, session and transaction numbers.
Test data, form fields and temporary file names.
Apps where many servers create records at the same time.

uuid-generator.p: Yes. Values are generated on your device using the browser's cryptographic random source; nothing is sent anywhere. The identifiers are entirely yours.

list: Are UUID and GUID the same? Yes — GUID is Microsoft's name for a UUID.
Can identifiers be changed? Every click produces fresh random values; generated lists are yours once copied.
How many values can I generate? As many as you like in a single batch.

unit-converter.p: A Unit Converter moves measurements between units for length, weight, volume, area and temperature. From centimeters to inches, kilograms to pounds, Celsius to Fahrenheit — hundreds of everyday conversions on one screen, useful for recipes, math homework, engineering and shopping.

list: Length: millimeter, centimeter, meter, kilometer, inch, foot, yard, mile.
Weight: milligram, gram, kilogram, ton, ounce, pound.
Volume: milliliter, centiliter, deciliter, liter, cubic meter, US gallon.
Area: square millimeter/centimeter/meter, hectare, square kilometer, acre.
Temperature: Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kelvin.

unit-converter.p: Yes. All conversions run in your browser; your values are never sent or stored. Free and account free.

list: What decimal separator can I use? Both comma and dot are accepted (e.g. 1,5 or 1.5).
Are results rounded? Values are rounded to six digits — accurate enough for everyday measurement.
Can more units be added? The five most common categories are supported; categories can be extended on request.

password-strength-checker.h: What is a Password Strength Checker?
password-strength-checker.p: A Password Strength Checker evaluates how resistant your password is to attack using an estimated entropy score. Length, character diversity and similarity to common passwords are checked, with the result shown from very weak to very strong and each missing requirement flagged.

password-strength-checker.h: What is entropy and why does it matter?
password-strength-checker.p: Entropy measures a password's unpredictability in bits. Every extra character and new character type multiplies the combinations a brute-force attack must try. An 8-character lower-case-only password is weak; the same length with digits and symbols is far stronger. This tool uses the same measure as our password generator.
Yes. The test runs entirely in your browser; your password is never sent, stored or logged. Test even your real passwords with confidence.

list: What length is enough? Aim for at least 12 characters; 16+ is safer.
Do you check the common-password list online? No — the list is embedded on your device.
What is the best password? A unique, long, unpredictable password stored in a password manager.

number-base-converter.h: What is a Number Base Converter?
number-base-converter.p: A Number Base Converter translates numbers between the four counting systems used in programming: binary (base 2), octal (base 8), decimal (base 10) and hexadecimal (base 16). Type a value, choose which base it is written in, and the tool shows all four representations at once — handy for color values, permission masks, memory addresses and bit-level work.

number-base-converter.h: Why do large numbers stay exact?
number-base-converter.p: The converter uses your browser's arbitrary-precision number type instead of floating-point math. Even values far beyond JavaScript's normal safe range convert digit-for-digit accurately and never round.

list: Binary (0, 1): bits, masks and bitwise operations in low-level programming.
Octal (0–7): classic Unix file permission masks used with chmod.
Decimal: ordinary everyday numbers.
Hexadecimal (0–9, A–F): CSS colors such as #FF8800, memory addresses and byte values.

number-base-converter.p: Yes. All conversions run in your browser; the number you type is never sent or stored. Free, no signup and no install.

regex-tester.p: A Regex Tester applies a regular expression to your text and shows the result live while you type. Matched pieces are highlighted, a match counter updates on every keystroke, and invalid patterns explain their error instead of failing silently.

list: g — global: find all matches instead of just the first.
i — ignore case: a matches both a and A.
m — multiline: ^ and $ match line starts and ends.
s — dot-all: . also matches newline characters.
u — unicode: enables unicode-aware escapes such as \p{...}.

regex-tester.h: How do I anchor my pattern?
regex-tester.p: Use ^ to anchor to the start of the text and $ to the end. Without anchors a pattern matches anywhere in the text. Add \b word boundaries for whole-word matching and use parentheses to capture groups you want to reuse.
Yes. Matching runs entirely on your device; your pattern and test text never leave the browser. Log lines, tokens or code samples can be tested here safely.

whitespace-cleaner.p: A Whitespace Cleaner normalizes spaces and line breaks in your text. Trim every line, collapse runs of spaces into one, drop empty lines or remove all whitespace — four cleaning modes on one screen that you can combine freely.

list: Trim lines: removes leading and trailing spaces from each line.
Collapse multiple spaces: turns repeated spaces or tabs into a single space.
Remove empty lines: deletes blank lines and closes gaps between paragraphs.
Remove all whitespace: strips every space, tab and newline from the text.
Cleaning text pasted from PDFs and emails that came with ragged spacing.
Normalizing configuration and CSV columns before reuse.
Compressing copy before conversion or measurement.
Preparing clean text for translation and word-count checks.

whitespace-cleaner.p: Yes. All cleaning happens in your browser; your text is never sent or stored. Free, no signup and completely client-side.

jwt-decoder.p: A JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe token that carries claims between two parties, used in authentication and authorization flows such as login sessions and API access. It consists of three base64url-encoded parts separated by dots.

list: Header: the token type and signing algorithm, e.g. alg: HS256.
Payload: the claims, e.g. sub, exp and other custom data.
Signature: verifies the token was not tampered with.

jwt-decoder.p: Yes. Decoding happens entirely in your browser; the token is never sent to any server. Note that decoding does not verify the signature — a JWT is readable by everyone who receives it.

json-csv-converter.h: What does the JSON ↔ CSV Converter do?
json-csv-converter.p: It converts a JSON array of objects (or a single object) into a CSV file with a header row, and converts CSV data back into a JSON array of objects. Fields containing commas, quotes or newlines are correctly quoted per RFC-4180 rules.

list: Migrating data between databases, spreadsheets and APIs.
Preparing CSV exports from API responses for Excel or Google Sheets.
Converting spreadsheet data into JSON for configuration files and scripts.

json-csv-converter.p: Yes. All conversion happens in your browser; your data is never uploaded or stored. Use it for private lists, reports and configuration data without worry.

json-csv-converter.h: When are flat rows not enough?
json-csv-converter.p: CSV works best for tabular data where every record has the same fields. Deeply nested JSON — objects inside arrays inside objects — does not translate cleanly to rows. Flatten with explicit keys (like user.address.city) so no information is lost, and rebuild from CSV only when the structure allows it.

Check the generated columns before you import: empty arrays become missing columns, and nested objects become dotted keys. Spend one minute verifying the mapping, and your spreadsheet or database import runs without surprises.

unix-timestamp-converter.p: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds that have elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC. Systems store times as these numbers because they are compact and timezone-independent; 1893456000, for example, equals 2030-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

list: Timestamp → date: enter e.g. 1893456000 and get the locale date and time (2030-01-01 00:00:00 UTC).
Date → timestamp: pick a date and time and get the exact epoch seconds; the value is treated as your local time.
Both results update instantly with your local timezone settings.

unix-timestamp-converter.p: Yes. All conversion runs in your browser; no value is ever sent or stored. No signup and no install needed.

duplicate-line-remover.h: What is a Duplicate Line Remover?
duplicate-line-remover.p: It scans your text line by line, removes repeated lines and keeps only the first occurrence of each one, preserving the original order. You instantly see how many lines were kept out of the total.

list: Cleaning email lists, membership databases and repeated contact rows.
Deduplicating imported product or inventory listings before upload.
Preparing unique keyword or URL lists for SEO and link building.

duplicate-line-remover.p: Yes. The process runs entirely in your browser; your list is never uploaded or stored. Paste anything private with confidence.

ai-token-counter.h: What is an AI Token Calculator?
ai-token-counter.p: It estimates the number of tokens your text will consume in an AI/LLM context window, alongside character, word and line counts. Model limits are quoted in tokens, so knowing your estimate helps you plan prompts, context and costs.

list: English text averages about 4 characters per token.
Turkish averages around 2.5 characters per token (the tool uses this ratio).
CJK characters (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) average about 1 token per character.

ai-token-counter.p: Yes. Counting runs entirely in your browser; your text is never sent to any server or API. Keep your prompts and sensitive drafts private while you plan token usage.

Models rarely count characters; they count tokens, which are pieces of words. Roughly one token equals one word in English and less than a word in many other languages. Counting tokens before sending text to a model tells you how long the request is and how much context you are using.

list: Punctuation and spaces often form their own tokens.
Rare or long words split into multiple tokens.
A token budget is shared between the prompt and the reply.
The same text can produce different counts on different models.

lorem-ipsum-generator.p: Lorem Ipsum is placeholder Latin text traced back to a work by the Roman statesman Cicero, popularized in the printing and typesetting industry since the 1960s. Because the words carry no real meaning, designers can judge a layout without being distracted by content.

list: Mockups and website designs that need neutral filler text.
Font and typesetting samples for print and web projects.
Testing responsive layouts before the final copy is written.
Presenting templates to clients ahead of the real text.

lorem-ipsum-generator.p: Yes. The text is generated entirely in your browser; your inputs and the generated paragraphs are never sent or stored. No signup, no install and completely free.

list: Layout mockups before the real copy is written.
Font and spacing tests with representative line lengths.
Editorial templates and print proofs that need sample text.
Documentation examples that must not distract with real content.

lorem-ipsum-generator.p: Lorem Ipsum is nonsense on purpose, so reviewers never mistake it for final copy. When you replace it with real text, check headings and long paragraphs too — awkward line breaks often show up only with authentic content.

tip-calculator.p: A Tip Calculator works out the tip on a bill, the total to pay and the share for each person when the bill is split evenly. Enter the bill amount, choose a tip percentage from 5% to 25% and set the number of people; the tip amount, total and per-person share update immediately.

tip-calculator.h: How is the per-person share calculated?
tip-calculator.p: The tool adds the bill and the tip, then divides by the number of people. A ₺400 bill with a 15% tip (₺60) split between 4 people comes to ₺115 per person; dividing the ₺460 total between 3 people gives ₺153.33 each.

list: 5% — a minimum gesture for basic service.
10% — common in casual or buffet service.
15% — the standard tip in many countries.
20% and 25% — for great service or larger groups.

discount-calculator.p: A Discount Calculator subtracts a discount percentage from an original price and reports the discount amount, the final price and the percentage that was saved. It is handy when comparing deals, preparing sales prices or checking whether a labeled discount really is a good deal.

The discount amount is the original price multiplied by the discount percentage; the final price is the original price minus that amount. An item priced at ₺250 with a 20% discount saves you ₺50, so you pay ₺200, and the "You save" value shows the 20% rate.

list: Shoppers comparing discounts and final prices before buying.
Shop owners preparing sale labels and promotions.
Students practicing percentage and discount math.

average-calculator.p: An Average Calculator reads the numbers you enter and computes five statistics at once — average, sum, count, minimum and maximum. Numbers can be separated by commas, spaces or new lines, and both comma and dot decimals are accepted.

For the numbers 10, 20 and 30, the average is 20, the sum is 60, the count is 3, the minimum is 10 and the maximum is 30. As another example, the average of 4.5 and 5.5 is 5. Results appear as soon as you press Calculate.

list: Grades: the average of exam or assignment scores.
Business: average order value or daily revenue.
Sports: average scores across games or seasons.
Personal tracking: average spending, distance or time.

dog-age-calculator.h: What is a Dog Age Calculator?
dog-age-calculator.p: A Dog Age Calculator converts your dog's age in years into an approximate human age using a modern, size-aware formula. Small, medium and large breeds age at different rates, so the tool lets you pick the right size before estimating.

The common formula counts the first year as about 15 human years, the second year as another 9, and then adds 4 to 5 human years per year depending on size. A 3-year-old medium dog therefore equals ≈15 + 9 + 4 = 28 human years.
Yes. The estimate is calculated entirely in your browser; the age and size you enter are never sent or stored. Free, no signup and completely client-side.

subnet-calculator.p: A Subnet Calculator takes an IPv4 address and a prefix length and computes the network address, broadcast address, netmask, total number of hosts and usable hosts for that subnet. It is used when planning IP ranges, VLANs, subnets in cloud services and container networks.
For 192.168.1.0/24 the network address is 192.168.1.0, the broadcast is 192.168.1.255, the netmask is 255.255.255.0, the total number of hosts is 256 and the usable hosts are 254.

subnet-calculator.h: Why are usable hosts fewer than total hosts?
subnet-calculator.p: The network address and the broadcast address are always reserved and cannot be assigned to a device. A /24 subnet therefore holds 256 addresses but offers 254 usable hosts.

px-rem-converter.h: What is a PX to REM converter?
px-rem-converter.p: A PX to REM converter translates pixel values into rem units and back, using the base font size you set. Because rem units scale relative to the root font size, text and spacing adjust smoothly when a user changes the browser's font settings.

px-rem-converter.h: How do rem values relate to pixels?
px-rem-converter.p: 1 rem equals the base font size: dividing pixels by the base gives rem, and multiplying rem by the base gives pixels. With a base of 16 px, 32 px becomes 2 rem and 1.5 rem becomes 24 px.

px-rem-converter.h: Why is 16 px the default base?
px-rem-converter.p: Major browsers use a default root font size of 16 px, which is why most projects start there. You can change it because some design systems adopt other bases such as 14 px or 10 px.

wcag-contrast-checker.p: The WCAG guidelines define how much contrast text must have against its background to stay readable, as a ratio that compares the relative luminance of the two colors. This tool computes the contrast ratio live and shows exactly which WCAG success criteria your color pair passes or fails.

list: AA Normal text: at least 4.5:1.
AA Large text: at least 3:1.
AAA Normal text: at least 7:1.
AAA Large text: at least 4.5:1.

wcag-contrast-checker.p: Yes. The ratio is computed locally in your browser; your colors never leave your device. No signup or install is required.

color-palette-generator.h: What is a Color Palette Generator?
color-palette-generator.p: A Color Palette Generator produces a set of harmoniously related colors from one base color. Analogous palettes step the hue around the color wheel, while monochrome palettes vary the lightness of the same hue. Choose 5, 7 or 9 colors and click any swatch to copy its HEX value.

list: Analogous: colors sitting next to each other on the color wheel — often used together in natural, calm designs.
Monochrome: tints and shades of one hue — safe for professional and minimal layouts.

color-palette-generator.p: Yes. Palettes are generated entirely in your browser; your base color is never sent anywhere. Everything stays on your device.

box-shadow-generator.h: What is a Box Shadow Generator?
box-shadow-generator.p: A Box Shadow Generator builds the CSS for a shadow under an element using simple sliders. You control the horizontal and vertical offset, blur radius, spread, opacity and color, and a preview box updates live with the exact style you are designing.

list: Offset X/Y: how far the shadow shifts right and down (negative values move it left and up).
Blur: how soft or sharp the shadow's edge is.
Spread: how much the shadow grows beyond the box size.
Opacity and color: the shadow's transparency and tint.

box-shadow-generator.p: Yes. The CSS is generated in your browser; your settings are never sent or saved. Copy the result and paste it straight into your stylesheet.

text-sorter.p: A Line Sorter takes the lines of any text — lists, CSV rows, names, URLs — and reorders them by the rule you choose. Sort alphabetically, by length or by numeric value, or shuffle the order entirely; the output is copied with one click.

list: A→Z / Z→A: alphabetical order with a Turkish-locale aware comparison.
Length: shortest lines first, useful for choosing short usernames or titles.
Numeric: compares parsed numbers when lines contain values like 2, 10, 200.
Shuffle: random order, for drawing turns or mixing a sequence.

text-sorter.p: Yes. Sorting runs entirely in your browser; your text is never sent or stored. No signup and completely free.

list: Alphabetical A→Z and Z→A for lists of names and words.
Numeric sorting for version numbers, scores or prices.
Ignore case so uppercase words do not cluster at the top.
Remove duplicates while sorting to clean repeated data.

text-sorter.p: Shuffled lists waste time: sorting finds duplicates instantly, makes comparisons easy and turns an unordered export into an organized reference. Sort a curriculum, a name list or a set of options before you publish anything.

list-shuffler.p: A List Randomizer mixes the items of a list so that every order is equally likely, or picks a single random item from it. Paste one item per line and choose Shuffle to reorder the whole list or Pick one to draw a single winner.

The tool uses the Fisher-Yates algorithm with a cryptographic-quality random source, so every possible order has the same probability. The result is fair — ideal for drawing raffles, assigning turns or randomizing test data.
Yes. Everything happens in your browser; your list is never sent anywhere. Runs fully client-side.

yaml-json-converter.h: What is a YAML ↔ JSON Converter?
yaml-json-converter.p: A YAML ↔ JSON Converter translates configuration data between the YAML text format and strict JSON syntax in both directions. Use it when porting config files, mocking APIs or switching between tools that expect one format or the other. Conversion runs with a small built-in YAML parser, so no data leaves your browser.

list: Config files: migrating .yml settings into JSON-based tools and CI pipelines.
Validation: checking hand-written YAML indentation or JSON commas.
Documentation: converting examples between the two formats.

yaml-json-converter.p: Yes. Parsing and conversion happen entirely in your browser; your data is never sent or stored. Configurations with secrets can be converted safely.

md5-file-checksum.h: What is an MD5 file checksum?
md5-file-checksum.p: An MD5 checksum is a 32-character fingerprint computed from every byte of a file. Even a tiny change produces a completely different digest, so comparing checksums is a quick way to confirm a file is exactly what it is supposed to be.

md5-file-checksum.h: What is a checksum used for?
list: Verifying downloads: comparing the digest published by a software vendor with the file you received.
Detecting corruption: confirming a copy was transferred without errors.
Deduplication: spotting identical files by their digest.

md5-file-checksum.p: Yes. The digest is computed entirely in your browser from the file bytes on your device; the file is never uploaded to any server, and the results are gone when you close the page.

image-compressor.p: An image compressor reduces the file size of a photo or graphic while keeping it visually sharp. This free online tool re-encodes your JPG, PNG or WebP image at the exact quality you choose, producing a much lighter file in seconds without any software to install.

list: Speeding up a slow website, blog or landing page
Shrinking photos before attaching them to email
Saving storage space on your phone or laptop
Meeting strict file size limits on upload forms
Is this image compressor free? Yes — the tool is completely free and unlimited.
Do my images get uploaded anywhere? No, compression runs entirely in your browser, so files never leave your device.
Which format compresses best? JPEG and WebP give the smallest photo files, while PNG keeps transparency and sharp edges.

image-compressor.p: There is no single perfect quality setting; the right value depends on the image and its use. Drop the quality slider slowly until the file is small enough but the image still looks clean at the size you display it. Preview the result inside the tool instead of guessing from the number alone.

list: Resize to the width that will actually be shown — extra pixels only add bytes.
Use JPEG for photos and WebP for a modern, smaller alternative.
Keep transparency in PNG only where it is really needed.
Aim for under 100 KB for content images; hero images can go a bit higher.

image-resizer.p: An image resizer changes the pixel dimensions of a picture, making it larger or smaller while keeping the content intact. This free online resizer lets you type an exact width or height, lock the aspect ratio, and download the result as a PNG or JPEG in seconds.

list: Fitting a photo into a blog header or social media post
Creating thumbnails from larger source images
Meeting exact pixel requirements on application forms
Preparing product shots for an online store
Does resizing reduce quality? Scaling down keeps images sharp, while scaling beyond the original size can soften detail.
Is the aspect ratio preserved? Yes — with keep aspect ratio enabled, changing one field updates the other automatically.
Which output format should I pick? Choose PNG for transparency and crisp edges, or JPEG when a smaller file matters more.

image-converter.p: An image converter changes a picture from one file format to another, such as JPEG to PNG or PNG to WebP. This free online converter re-encodes your file right in the browser with a quality slider, so you can balance clarity and file size before downloading the result.

list: Turning PNG screenshots into much smaller JPEG files
Switching to WebP for faster, lighter websites
Preparing images that only accept one specific format
Flattening transparency by converting to JPEG
Which image format is best? JPEG suits photos, PNG preserves transparency and sharp lines, and WebP modern compression for both.
Can I control the output quality? Yes — the quality slider applies to JPEG and WebP so you can trade a little detail for a smaller file.
Are converted files stored? No — conversion happens in your browser and the new file downloads straight to your device.

image-to-base64.p: Base64 encoding turns a binary image into plain text so it can be embedded directly in HTML, CSS or JSON. This free online tool converts your picture into a data URL instantly and shows the file size plus the full encoded length, so you know exactly what you are about to paste.

list: Inlining small icons directly in CSS or HTML
Embedding images in JSON or API payloads
Sharing an image as text in chat or a support ticket
Avoiding extra image requests on a landing page
Is this Base64 converter free? Yes, it is completely free and you can convert as many images as you like.
Why is the Base64 string longer than the file? Encoding adds about a third in overhead, so a 30 KB image becomes roughly 40 KB of text.
Does my image get uploaded? No, the conversion uses your browser's FileReader and the data never leaves your device.

image-color-picker.h: What Is an Image Color Picker?
image-color-picker.p: An image color picker samples the exact color of any pixel in a picture and returns its HEX and RGB values. This free online tool shows a live swatch as you move the mouse, and every click saves the color to a palette you can copy straight into your design tool or stylesheet.

list: Matching brand colors from a logo or screenshot
Building a palette from a photo you love
Checking color pairs for accessible, readable designs
Copying exact HEX codes for CSS or design files
How do I pick a color? Upload an image, hover over the canvas to preview a pixel, then click to add it to your picked colors.
Is the image color picker free? Yes — it is free to use and runs entirely in your browser with no account needed.
How do I copy a saved color? Press the copy button next to any color in the list to put its HEX code on the clipboard.

slug-generator.p: A URL slug is the human-readable part of a link that identifies a page, such as the words that appear after your domain in a blog post URL. Clean slugs help search engines and visitors understand what a page is about before they even click.

slug-generator.h: How to Use This Slug Generator
list: Type or paste any title, sentence, or keyword phrase.
Choose a separator: hyphen, underscore, or no separator at all.
Toggle ASCII-only output to transliterate accented and Turkish characters.
Copy the finished slug and paste it into your CMS or router.
Why should slugs be lowercase? Lowercase slugs avoid duplicate URLs caused by case differences and are easier to share and remember.
What separator is best? Hyphens are the most common choice for SEO, but underscores work fine when your system expects them.
Does this tool send my text anywhere? No. Everything runs locally in your browser, so your input never leaves your device.
Lowercase letters and hyphens — no spaces or special characters.
Short: three to five words are usually enough.
Include the main keyword for your page.
Be stable: change the slug rarely, because URLs are indexed.

slug-generator.p: Search engines read the URL as a relevance signal and users read it before they click. A clear slug like /how-to-bake-bread tells both exactly what the page covers. Keep the same slug when the title changes, or set a redirect when you must rewrite it.

meta-tag-generator.p: Meta tags are often the first thing visitors read about your page. A compelling title and description can significantly raise your click-through rate from search results, while Open Graph and Twitter tags control how your link looks when it is shared on social networks.

list: A HTML title tag and meta description for search engines.
Open Graph tags for Facebook and LinkedIn, and a type field for websites or articles.
Twitter Card tags that control how your link appears in tweets.
A Google-style preview so you can judge length and wording at a glance.
How long should my title be? Aim for about 50 to 60 characters so search engines do not cut it off.
What is the ideal description length? Between 140 and 160 characters gives you room for a full message.
Do I need an image for Twitter cards? A large image card looks best, but the tool falls back to a summary card without one.
Title (under 60 characters) and meta description (around 155).
Canonical URL to point search engines at the preferred version.
Open Graph (og:title, og:image) to control social shares.
Charset and viewport so mobile browsers render correctly.

meta-tag-generator.p: Metadata only matters when it shows up the way you planned. Run the result through a search snippet preview to see how the title and description behave, then fine-tune wording until the snippet looks compelling.

keyword-density-checker.p: Keyword density is the percentage of times a word or phrase appears in a text compared with the total number of words. A balanced density signals relevance to search engines without looking like keyword stuffing.

list: Total words counts every token found in your text.
Unique words shows how many distinct terms appear.
Each row lists a word, its occurrence count, and its share of the whole text.
Lower the minimum length filter to include short words such as prepositions.
What is a healthy keyword density? There is no fixed number, but repeating a key term around one to two percent of the time usually reads naturally.
Does punctuation affect the count? Yes, the tool strips punctuation so forms like word and word. count as the same term.
Is my text uploaded anywhere? No, the analysis runs entirely in your browser.

keyword-density-checker.p: There is no exact rule, but a keyword appearing naturally once or twice per paragraph is usually sane. Very high repetition triggers readability problems and looks like stuffing. Use the checker to stay consistent, not to chase an exact percentage.

Search engines evaluate whether a page truly covers a topic, not whether a phrase shows up a specific number of times. Write the best answer you can, then use the density tool to catch accidental overuse or a forgotten main term.

serp-preview.p: Google shows a blue title followed by a short description under your page address. Both are usually truncated when they run too long, which can cut your message in half and lower click-through rates.

list: Keep the title at or below 60 characters to avoid truncation.
Keep the description at or below 160 characters.
Put your most important keyword near the start of the title.
Write a description that promises a clear benefit to the reader.
Does Google always use my title tag? Not always. It may rewrite titles it considers too long, too short, or stuffed with keywords.
What do the green and orange counters mean? Green means you are within the recommended length, orange means the text will likely be cut off.
Is the preview pixel perfect? It is a close approximation of Google's desktop layout, updated live as you type.

serp-preview.p: Titles that are too long get cut off mid-word, and long descriptions end with an ellipsis. Testing a full-width preview shows exactly where the cut happens, so you can keep the important words inside the visible part.

serp-preview.h: How to write a snippet that gets clicks
list: Lead with the value: what the page offers or solves.
Use the keyword early, but read naturally.
Stay inside the visible limits — don't waste pixels on branding.
End with a concrete promise instead of a vague phrase.

readability-score.h: What Is the Flesch Reading Ease Score?
readability-score.p: The Flesch Reading Ease formula rates a text from 0 to 100 based on average sentence length and average syllables per word. Higher scores mean the text is easier to read, while lower scores point to dense, academic writing.

list: 90 to 100: very easy, understood by an average 11-year-old.
70 to 89: easy, works well for blogs and general audiences.
50 to 69: fairly difficult, suits informed readers on focused topics.
Below 50: difficult, consider shorter sentences and simpler words.
Does this work for Turkish text? Yes, the syllable counter uses a vowel-group heuristic that handles Turkish vowels correctly.
What grade level should I aim for? Most web content reads best around a seventh to ninth grade level.
Is my text stored? No, all calculations happen locally in your browser.

text-diff.h: What is a text diff checker?
text-diff.p: It compares two documents line by line and aligns them so matching lines stay paired. Lines that appear only in the first text are marked as removed, lines that appear only in the second are marked as added, while identical lines remain unhighlighted.

list: Paste the original text into the left box and the new version into the right box.
Review the side-by-side view: amber removals on the left, green additions on the right.
Check the summary tiles for total, added, removed and unchanged line counts.
Is my text uploaded anywhere? No — the comparison runs entirely in your browser and your text never leaves your device.
Is the comparison case-sensitive? Yes, lines are compared exactly; a line that only differs in capitalization counts as changed.
How are large texts handled? The comparison is line-based, so pairing stays correct across thousands of lines.

html-entity-converter.p: HTML entities are codes that start with an ampersand and end with a semicolon, for example & for &. They let you safely insert characters that have special meaning in HTML, like angle brackets, quotes and ampersands, without breaking the markup.

list: Reserved characters & < > " ' are always encoded.
Common accents: é becomes é, and the Turkish letters ç, ğ, ı, ö, ş, ü and İ get proper entities.
All other characters are passed through unchanged.
Is my data sent anywhere? No — encoding and decoding run entirely in your browser.
Why does ' become '? The apostrophe is encoded as a numeric entity so it is safe inside single-quoted attributes.
Can I decode any entity? Yes, standard named and numeric entities are decoded back to their characters.

morse-converter.p: Morse code encodes letters, digits and punctuation as sequences of dots and dashes. It was originally used for telegraph communication, where each character is a timed signal of short and long pulses.

list: Text to Morse: letters become dot-dash sequences separated by spaces; words are separated by a slash (/).
Morse to text: each symbol is read back to its letter; a slash marks a word boundary.
Supported characters are A–Z, 0–9 and the punctuation . , ? ! & ( ) and -.
Can Turkish letters be translated? No — Turkish characters such as ç and ş are not part of standard Morse and are left as-is.
Why are words separated by /? It is the widely used convention for representing a space between words in Morse text.
Is my message sent to a server? No, all translation happens locally in your browser.

morse-converter.p: Morse replaces each letter with a pattern of dots (short) and dashes (long), separated by pauses. Letters are separated by one pause, words by three. The timing is what makes Morse readable — not just which marks exist.

list: Learn a few letters first — start with SOS, the most famous pattern.
Convert your own name to see real text become Morse.
Translate to Morse, copy the pattern, and recite it from memory.
Use it for fun projects, puzzles and learning about early radio.

text-reverser.p: It rearranges the characters or words of your text in three ways: reverse every character, reverse the order of whole words while keeping letters readable, or reverse each word individually while keeping the sentence order.

text-reverser.h: What is each mode good for?
list: Reverse all characters: classic mirror-style text used for puzzles and challenges.
Reverse word order: turns a phrase into its words read backwards, letters untouched.
Reverse each word: flips the letters inside every word but keeps the words in the same order.
Does it keep whitespace and punctuation? Yes, spaces, punctuation and line breaks keep their positions as closely as possible.
Is my text sent anywhere? No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Are Turkish characters supported? Yes, all Unicode text is reversed correctly.

fancy-text-generator.h: What is a bold & italic text generator?
fancy-text-generator.p: It replaces each letter and digit of your text with its Unicode mathematical style equivalent. Characters look bold, italic, bold-italic or monospace in any app that supports them, without you applying any formatting.

fancy-text-generator.h: Where can I use styled text?
list: Social media bios, usernames and captions that do not offer a bold button.
Chat messages, forum posts and comments that only accept plain text.
Titles, signatures and highlights inside documents or emails.
Why does the style disappear in some apps? The characters are real Unicode symbols, but apps that lack glyph support fall back to a plain look.
Are all characters converted? Only A–Z, a–z and 0–9 have styled equivalents; Turkish accents and symbols stay untouched.
Where does the conversion happen? Entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

caesar-cipher.p: A substitution cipher where each letter of the alphabet is replaced by the letter a fixed number of positions later. With a shift of 3, A becomes D, B becomes E and so on; it is one of the oldest known encryption techniques.

list: Choose Encrypt or Decrypt to set the direction of the transformation.
Drag the shift slider from 1 to 25 to pick how far letters move.
Hit ROT13 to jump straight to shift 13, where encrypting and decrypting are the same operation.
Which characters are changed? Only A–Z and a–z are shifted; numbers, accents, Turkish letters and symbols stay untouched.
Is ROT13 secure? No, it is not a form of real encryption — like all Caesar shifts it is trivially breakable.
Where is the work done? Entirely in your browser; your text is never uploaded.

gpa-calculator.p: This free tool lets you enter each of your courses with its credit amount and letter grade, then computes a weighted GPA on the standard 4.0 scale used by most universities. A+ and A both count as 4.0, followed by A- 3.7, B+ 3.3 and so on down to F. You can also switch on a 100-scale average that estimates each grade's typical percentage.

list: Click Add course to create rows for every course you have or plan to take.
Set the credits for each course (default 1) and pick the grade from the dropdown.
Read your weighted GPA, total credits and optional 100-scale average.
Copy the result with one click to share or store it.

Is A+ worth more than A? On the standard 4.0 scale both A+ and A equal 4.0 points. Some universities use a 4.3 scale that adds extra weight to A+, but this calculator follows the common 4.0 convention.

What does 'weighted' mean? All grades are multiplied by their course's credit amount before the average is taken. A strong grade in a high-credit course therefore affects your GPA more than a grade in a low-credit one.

Is the 100-scale average accurate? The 100-scale average uses each letter grade's typical percentage, so it is an estimate. Your school may apply a different conversion table, especially for A+ or F grading.

loan-emi-calculator.p: EMI (Equated Monthly Installment) is the fixed amount you pay each month to repay a loan with interest. This free calculator uses the standard formula P × r × (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1), where P is the principal, r the monthly interest rate and n the number of months, so you always see an accurate monthly payment.

list: Enter the loan amount in your currency, e.g. 500000.
Type the annual interest rate in percent and the term in months.
Read the monthly payment, total payment and total interest cards.
Open the amortization table to see principal, interest and balance month by month.
How is the monthly rate calculated? The annual interest rate is divided by 12 to get the monthly rate. For example, an annual rate of 24% becomes a 2% monthly rate before the EMI formula is applied.

Why is total interest almost as high as the principal? Interest is charged on the remaining balance each month. Early payments go mostly toward interest, so the total interest can be high for long terms or high rates.
Does the calculator include fees? No. It computes only principal and interest. Banks often add origination fees, insurance or other costs that are not included in the EMI here.

calorie-bmr-calculator.p: BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) is the energy your body burns at complete rest, and TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) adds the calories you burn through activity. This free calculator computes BMR with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation — men: 10×weight + 6.25×height - 5×age + 5, women: -161 — then multiplies it by your chosen activity factor.

list: Select your sex and enter age, height in centimeters and weight in kilograms.
Choose an activity level that matches your typical weekly exercise.
Read your BMR and TDEE calorie cards, then check the three goal rows.
Copy your TDEE with one click to use it in your own plan.

Which activity level should I pick? Be honest about your real week. Sedentary means little exercise, light is 1-3 days, moderate is 3-5 days, active is 6-7 days and very active includes hard training or a physical job. Choosing too high a level often overestimates your burn.

Why does the calculator suggest -500 calories? One kilogram of body fat holds roughly 7,700 kcal, so cutting about 500 kcal a day means around -0.5 kg (about one pound) per week — a common, sustainable weight-loss target.

Can I trust these numbers exactly? Mifflin-St Jeor is accurate for most adults, but every formula is an estimate. Muscle mass, genetics and daily variation all affect real energy needs, so treat the result as a starting point.

body-fat-calculator.p: This free calculator uses the U.S. Navy circumference method, which estimates body fat from height plus neck, waist and (for women) hip measurements. For men: 86.010 × log10(waist - neck) - 70.041 × log10(height) + 36.76. For women: 163.205 × log10(waist + hip - neck) - 97.684 × log10(height) - 78.387.

list: Select your sex and enter height, neck, waist and, for women, hip in centimeters.
Optional: add your weight to also get your fat mass in kilograms.
Read your body fat percentage, ACE category and explanatory note.
Check the category table below for men and women ranges.

How accurate is the U.S. Navy formula? When measured carefully, its error is typically around 3-4% compared with laboratory methods such as hydrostatic weighing. Keep measurements consistent and not too tight for the best result.

What do the ACE categories mean? They follow the American Council on Exercise ranges: essential fat, athletes, fitness, average and obese. They are general guides and your ideal range depends on age, sport and personal goals.

Why is the hip measurement only for women? Women store proportionally more fat around the hips and thighs, so the formula uses waist plus hip minus neck for them. Men can be estimated from the waist alone.

ideal-weight-calculator.p: This free calculator reports the two most common ideal weight formulas. Devine gives 50 + 2.3 × (height in inches - 60) for men and 45.5 + 2.3 × (height in inches - 60) for women. Robinson gives 52 + 1.9 × (...) for men and 49 + 1.7 × (...) for women. It also shows the healthy range for a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9.

list: Select your sex and enter your height in centimeters.
Optional: enter your current weight to compare it with the healthy range.
Read the Devine and Robinson ideal weight values.
See the healthy BMI weight range and a color hint for your position in it.

Which ideal weight should I trust? The formulas were built for height-based estimates on adult populations, so small differences between them are normal. The healthy BMI range is often the better practical target because it acknowledges a span of healthy weights.

Why do men and women get different values? On average women have less lean mass and more essential body fat at the same height, so both formulas start from a lower base for women (45.5-49 kg instead of 50-52 kg) and the Robinson slope is smaller.
What is the healthy BMI range? A BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 is considered normal weight by the WHO. The calculator converts that BMI range to a weight range in kilograms based on your height.

sleep-calculator.h: How does the sleep calculator work?
sleep-calculator.p: A full sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes and goes through light sleep, deep sleep and REM sleep. This free calculator adds about 15 minutes for falling asleep and then works backwards from your wake-up time — or forwards from your bedtime — to recommend schedules that end at the natural end of the 5th or 6th cycle.

list: Choose the wake-up mode to get recommended bedtimes, or the bedtime mode for wake-up suggestions.
Pick a time with the time input.
Read the suggestions for 5 and 6 sleep cycles.
Copy the full list with one click and follow the schedule that fits your life.

Why are 5 or 6 cycles recommended? Waking up inside deep sleep makes you groggy, while waking between cycles leaves you more alert. With 5 cycles you sleep about 7.5 hours and with 6 about 9 hours, plus roughly 15 minutes to fall asleep.

Do I have to start in bed exactly at the suggested time? No. The suggested bedtime is when you should aim to fall asleep about 15 minutes later. Falling asleep a few minutes off is fine — consistency matters more than a perfect minute.

Can I use it if I sleep less than 5 cycles? It works with any wake-up or bedtime you enter. Staying within complete cycles is ideal, but a 4-cycle night is still calculated correctly if that is what your schedule allows.

cron-tester.h: What is a Cron Expression Tester?
cron-tester.p: A Cron Expression Tester checks a five-field cron expression such as 0 9 * * MON-FRI and explains what each field matches in plain language. It then scans forward minute by minute from now to find the next five exact run times, which you can copy as ISO-style or localized timestamps.

cron-tester.h: How do the five fields work?
list: Minute (0–59): picks the minute of each hour; */5 matches every 5 minutes.
Hour (0–23): selects which hours run; 9-17 means 09:00 through 17:00.
Day of month (1–31): selects days such as 1,15,31 or a range like 1-15.
Month (1–12 or JAN–DEC): restricts the expression to certain months; names like JAN-DEC are accepted.
Day of week (0–7 or SUN–SAT): 0 and 7 both mean Sunday; MON-FRI matches weekdays.
What syntax does the tool accept? Standard five-field cron syntax: *, */n, a-b, a-b/n and comma-separated lists like 0,15,30,45.
Are month and weekday names case-sensitive? No — MON, mon and Mon are all accepted and can be mixed freely with numbers.
Do day-of-month and day-of-week combine? Yes, like classic cron: when both are restricted, a date matches when either field matches.

aes-encryption.p: This tool encrypts your text with AES-GCM 256, a modern authenticated cipher, using a key derived from your password with PBKDF2 (100,000 iterations). The same password can decrypt the stored value back, and everything runs in your browser with nothing uploaded.

aes-encryption.h: Why is the output in three parts?
list: Salt: random bytes that make the derived key unique even for the same password.
IV: a fresh random initialization vector generated for every encryption.
Ciphertext: the encrypted bytes plus an integrity tag so tampering is always detected.
All three are base64-encoded and joined as base64(salt).base64(iv).base64(ciphertext); decrypt parses this exact format.
Can you decrypt my data? No — the password is required to derive the key, and encryption happens entirely in the browser; the tool never sees your plaintext or password.
Why is it not instant? PBKDF2 runs 100,000 iterations on purpose to make brute-force attacks expensive; that delay is what keeps the encryption strong.
A decrypt error says wrong password or bad format — what now? Either the password does not match, the value was edited, or the three base64 parts are missing.

random-string-generator.h: What is a Random String Generator?
random-string-generator.p: A Random String Generator instantly produces random text from the character types you enable: uppercase, lowercase, digits and symbols. It uses the browser crypto.getRandomValues API with unbiased sampling, so results suit tokens, salts, one-time codes and test data.

list: Uppercase (A–Z): capital letters.
Lowercase (a–z): lower-case letters.
Digits (0–9): numbers.
Symbols (!@#$…): punctuation and special characters.
Length: any value from 1 to 128 characters; you can regenerate as many times as you like.
Is it really random? Yes — values come from crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographic-quality source; every generation is fresh and independent.
Can the same string appear twice? Randomness means a repeat is technically possible, but with long strings the chance is astronomically small.
Is the result stored or uploaded? No — generation happens locally in your browser and nothing is sent to any server.

random-string-generator.h: What to use random strings for
list: Password salts and reset tokens that must never repeat.
Temporary identifiers for test data and fixtures.
Example keys in documentation and demos.
Unique name suffixes when copy-pasting between environments.

random-string-generator.p: Longer strings with a bigger alphabet give far more combinations. For security-critical values like salts or tokens, prefer 32+ characters from the full character set. For display or test purposes, shorter strings are fine and easier to type.

jwt-generator.p: A JWT Generator builds a signed JSON Web Token from three parts you control: a header that declares the signing algorithm, a payload with your claims, and a secret. The token is formed as header.payload.signature, where the signature proves the first two parts have not been altered since signing.

list: Header: small JSON declaring the algorithm (for example HS256), base64url-encoded without padding.
Payload: the claims — JSON such as issuer, subject and expiry, also base64url-encoded.
Signature: the HMAC-SHA256 digest of header.payload, keyed with your secret.
The final token is header.payload.signature, ready to copy into a test, curl command or another service.

jwt-generator.h: What role does the secret play?
jwt-generator.p: The secret is the private key that signs the token. The server that issues and verifies the token keeps the same secret. Anyone with the secret can forge tokens, so treat it like a password — never put it in client-side code or a public repository.

jwt-generator.h: When should you use a JWT?
list: Stateless authentication: the server verifies a signature instead of storing sessions.
API access: short-lived access tokens in Authorization headers.
Single sign-on between applications that share a signing secret.
Remember: JWTs are signed, not encrypted — never put passwords or personal data in the payload unless you add an extra layer of encryption.

jwt-generator.h: How to use the FreetoolsY generator
jwt-generator.p: Paste your header and payload JSON, type your secret and press generate. You get the complete token plus the three parts shown separately, with a copy button for the result. Everything is signed in your browser with the Web Crypto API — no part of the token or your secret ever leaves the page.

currency-converter.p: A Currency Converter converts an amount from one currency to another using reference rates you can adjust. It is useful for travel budgets, online shopping in foreign stores, freelance invoices and checking prices when an amount is quoted in another money.

currency-converter.h: Where do the rates come from?
currency-converter.p: The tool ships with fixed reference rates that you can override manually with the latest rate you know. Because markets change every second, double-check your figures against the spot rate when the exact amount matters.

list: Choose the source and target currencies.
Enter the amount or adjust the reference rate if yours differs.
Read the converted result and the reverse rate in one glance.
Can I update the rate? Yes — edit the base rate field before converting.
Do I need an internet connection? No, everything runs in your browser.
Is the exchange rate live? The initial values are reference rates; update them for the current market value.

compound-interest-calculator.p: Compound interest means your returns earn their own returns. This calculator shows how an initial deposit grows over the years when interest is added, with optional monthly contributions and a full yearly breakdown.

list: Starting amount and monthly deposit.
Annual rate and compounding frequency (yearly, monthly, daily).
Investment length in years or months.

compound-interest-calculator.p: The yearly breakdown shows exactly how much comes from contributions and how much is earned interest each year. Use it to compare scenarios, such as saving more each month versus getting a higher rate.

list: How does compounding frequency change? Pick daily, monthly or yearly in the settings and the table recalculates.
Is this tax-adjusted? No — the result is gross growth before any taxes or fees.
Is my data safe? All calculations happen in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

salary-calculator.h: What is a Net Salary Calculator?
salary-calculator.p: A Net Salary Calculator estimates how much of your gross wage you take home after SGK, unemployment insurance and income tax deductions. It follows Turkey's payroll system and gives you monthly and annual summaries.

list: Gross-to-net conversion with SGK and unemployment deductions.
Income tax according to the progressive brackets and the minimum wage deduction threshold.
Monthly, annual and per-pay-period breakdowns.

salary-calculator.p: Enter your gross wage and see the net salary instantly. Compare offers or check how a raise changes your take-home amount before you sign anything.

list: Is this number exact? It is an estimate; the final figure depends on your exact situation and employer choices.
Does it include bonuses? Overtime, bonuses and other perks are not covered.
Are tax brackets up to date? The calculator uses the current bracket logic; verify against the latest official rates.

sql-formatter.p: A SQL Formatter turns messy SQL into clean, readable queries — or compresses it into one compact line. Choose your indentation and keyword casing and format instantly in your browser.

list: Debugging long stored procedures with consistent alignment.
Sharing readable queries with teammates.
Preparing compact SQL for blog posts, chat or small tool windows.

sql-formatter.p: Pick the number of indent spaces and whether keywords are uppercase, lowercase or left as written. The Minify option strips whitespace for a single-line output.

list: Does it work for SQL Server, MySQL and Postgres? Yes — the formatter is generic and handles the common dialects.
Is my query sent to a server? No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Can I format without changing the query logic? Yes, formatting only changes whitespace and casing.

json-xml-converter.h: What is a JSON to XML Converter?
json-xml-converter.p: A JSON to XML Converter changes JSON data into XML and XML into JSON, in both directions. Arrays are preserved as repeated elements and XML attributes are supported, so most real-world documents convert cleanly.

list: Paste JSON or XML on the left, choose the direction and click Convert.
Review the output and the error message if conversion fails.
Copy the result with one click.

json-xml-converter.p: Documents with attributes round-trip using an @attr convention, and repeated elements become arrays. If a document is invalid, the tool points to the problem so you can fix it and convert again.

list: Is my data stored? No — everything is processed in your browser.
Does it keep the order of attributes? Attribute order is preserved when converting back.
Can I convert very large files? Yes, the conversion runs directly in your browser with no size limit.

markdown-html-converter.h: What is a Markdown to HTML Converter?
markdown-html-converter.p: A Markdown to HTML Converter writes HTML from Markdown or translates HTML back into Markdown, with a live preview so you see the result as you go.

list: Turning Markdown notes into HTML for emails or website editors.
Converting existing HTML pages back into clean Markdown.
Checking how a snippet will render before publishing.

markdown-html-converter.p: Yes. The conversion happens entirely in your browser, so pasted content never leaves your device — safe for drafts and internal documents.

list: Which Markdown is supported? Common syntax: headings, lists, code, tables and links.
Does HTML-to-Markdown handle complex layouts? It converts standard formatting; very complex nested markup may stay partly as HTML.
Do I need internet? No, the tool works offline in your browser.

hmac-generator.p: An HMAC Generator computes an HMAC-SHA256 or HMAC-SHA512 signature for your message using a secret key, and shows the result in hex and Base64. It is commonly used to verify the integrity and origin of API requests.

list: Paste your message text and your secret key.
Choose SHA-256 or SHA-512 as the hash function.
Copy the resulting signature in hex or Base64.

hmac-generator.p: The signature depends on the exact bytes of your message. Use the same signing settings as the service you are talking to, and never paste production secrets on untrusted machines — this tool runs entirely in your browser.

list: Is HMAC the same as simple hashing? No — HMAC keys the hash with a secret, so it proves authenticity, not just integrity.
Does it work on files? Not directly; hash the file contents first, then sign the hash.
Is my secret key safe? The key is processed locally in your browser and never transmitted.

html-table-generator.h: What is an HTML Table Generator?
html-table-generator.p: An HTML Table Generator creates ready-to-paste HTML table code from your rows, columns and pasted data, with a live preview so you see the final look before copying.

list: Set a blank grid with your chosen number of rows and columns.
Paste TSV data (for example, from Excel or Google Sheets).
Add a table caption and optional borders.

html-table-generator.p: Hand-writing table markup is tedious. This tool generates clean, ready-to-paste code you can drop into a CMS, editor or email template, then restyle with your own CSS.

list: Can I include a header row? Yes, the first row can be marked as table headers.
Does it support merged cells? Not automatically; the generator covers the common flat tables.
Where is the code produced? In your browser — nothing is uploaded.

favicon-generator.p: A Favicon Generator draws a favicon from a letter or short text plus your colors, then lets you download it as PNG or ICO. Use it to give a site a recognizable browser-tab icon without a graphics program.

list: Type the character or text you want on the icon and choose the text color.
Pick the background color (optionally with rounded corners).
Download as PNG or ICO and point your head at it.

favicon-generator.p: Favicons are tiny — keep the text short and the colors high-contrast. Test it in both light and dark tabs so the icon stays visible.

list: What is the difference between ICO and PNG? ICO keeps multiple sizes for older browsers; PNG is simpler and supported by modern ones.
Does it read my logo file? The generator draws from text; use an image editor for a custom logo.
Is my data private? Everything is generated client-side.

image-crop.p: An Image Cropper lets you trim any image to the exact area you want by dragging a selection box directly in the browser — no uploads, no signup.

list: Drop or select an image file.
Drag the handles to frame the part you want to keep.
Download the cropped image as PNG or JPEG.

image-crop.p: The crop removes everything outside the selection without recompressing the rest, so the sharpness of the kept area is preserved for web use.

list: Can I set an exact pixel size? Crop visually first, then optionally resize the result with the site's image resizer.
What formats are supported? Common image formats including JPEG, PNG and WebP.
Is my photo uploaded? No — all processing happens locally in your browser.

image-watermark.p: An Image Watermark places a logo or image stamp over your photo at the position and opacity you choose, protecting your content or showing ownership on social shares.

list: Load the base image and the watermark image (a logo or signature).
Set the position, size and opacity.
Download the resulting image as PNG.

image-watermark.p: Lower opacity and a corner position keep photos clean while still identifying the source. Export as PNG so the composite keeps a transparent background where needed.

list: Can I add text instead of a logo? Use this tool with the watermark saved as an image, or use a dedicated text tool.
Does it resize the original? The output size follows the original image.
Is my content uploaded? No, everything runs in your browser.

jsonld-generator.p: A JSON-LD Generator builds schema.org structured data for common types — Article, Product, FAQPage, Event, Person and more — ready to paste into your page head for rich results.

list: Pick a structured data type.
Fill in the fields shown in plain language.
Copy the generated JSON-LD and paste it inside a script tag in your head.

jsonld-generator.p: Structured data helps search engines understand your content and can unlock rich results such as star ratings, FAQs and event listings — a small snippet with real visibility payoff.

list: Do I need to be a developer? No — the fields are labeled in plain language.
Does it produce valid JSON? Yes, the output is always valid JSON; verify it in Google's result-testing tools.
Where does processing happen? In your browser, so your content stays private.

hreflang-generator.p: An Hreflang Generator creates hreflang link tags and x-default entries for multilingual sites, then formats them for your head or your XML sitemap — no more hand-typing URL lists.

list: Enter the URL of each language version of the page.
Choose the output format: HTML link tags or sitemap-XML blocks.
Copy the output and paste it into your head or sitemap.

hreflang-generator.p: Every language version should list all of its siblings and add a matching x-default. The generator includes x-default so search engines see a complete, self-consistent signal.

list: Do I need hreflang on every page? Add it to every localized URL and mirror the tags on each version.
Do you validate the URLs? The tool formats the entries; verify the final code in Search Console.
Is my URL list uploaded? No, it is built locally in your browser.

robots-txt-generator.p: A Robots.txt Generator writes robots.txt content from presets — like allow-all or block-all — plus your own allow and disallow rules, ready to drop into your site root.

list: Start from a preset (allow all, block all, or block search crawlers).
Add specific paths to allow or disallow for each user agent.
Copy the final text into your /robots.txt file.

robots-txt-generator.p: robots.txt steers well-behaved crawlers; it is not a security barrier. Keep disallow rules to paths that should stay out of search results, and test changes in Search Console afterwards.

list: Which hostname should I use? Place one robots.txt at the root of the exact host you serve.
Can it point to a sitemap? Yes — the generated text includes a sitemap line.
Is the file stored anywhere? No, it is produced locally in your browser.

wheel-of-names.h: What is a Wheel of Names?
wheel-of-names.p: A Wheel of Names spins a colorful wheel carrying your list of names, then lands on a random winner. Perfect for classroom picks, prize draws, team assignments and friendly raffles.

list: Add each entry as a line in the names box.
Spin the wheel and watch it settle on a winner.
Remove the winner and spin again for a second prize.

wheel-of-names.h: Draws that are fair and fun
wheel-of-names.p: The spin is random, so the result is impartial — and the colorful wheel looks great on a projector or big screen while the tension builds.

list: Can I use pictures instead of names? The wheel supports text entries.
Can I pick several winners? Yes — remove a winner from the list and spin again.
Does it need internet? No, it runs entirely in your browser.

random-number-generator.h: What is a Random Number Generator?
random-number-generator.p: A Random Number Generator produces random numbers within any range you choose, with or without repeats. It is handy for lottery picks, sample selection, dice-like rolls and testing.

list: Enter the minimum and maximum of the range.
Choose how many numbers you want and whether repeats are allowed.
Generate, then copy the list or sort it.

random-number-generator.h: True randomness lives in the browser
random-number-generator.p: The generator uses the browser's cryptographic randomness source, so every draw is independent and cannot be predicted.

list: Can repeats be disabled? Yes — switch to unique-only mode when each number may appear once.
Does it support negative numbers? Yes, choose any range.
Is the result stored? No, numbers are generated locally.

stopwatch-timer.h: What is a Stopwatch and Timer?
stopwatch-timer.p: A Stopwatch measures elapsed time with lap splits, while a Timer counts down from a set duration and rings when finished. Two tools for timing craft, cooking, workouts and games.

list: Stopwatch: tap Start, record laps, and read the total and split times.
Timer: set minutes and seconds, then press Start.
Reset clears the current mode; the timer beeps when it finishes.

stopwatch-timer.p: Times are based on real clock time, so even if the tab is hidden the durations stay correct.

list: Can I record laps? Yes — as many as you need, kept in a scrollable list with splits and totals.
Does it ring on completion? The timer plays a short beep at zero.
Is anything transmitted? No — everything runs locally in your browser.

The site uses cookies to remember preferences (such as theme choice) and to measure service quality. You can allow or block cookies from your browser settings at any time; blocking them does not stop most tools from working.
